pr_title: opt: table statistics include information about the size of columns
pr_body:
In this change we add a new field, `avgSize`, to
`system.table_statistics`. The `avgSize` is the average size in bytes
of the column(s) for which the statistics are collected. In a future PR,
we will use the `avgSize` to more accurately cost operators such as
scans.

We try to use the encoded column size to compute the average size, but
if the encoding is not available for some reason we use the decoded
`Datum` size.

For example, the following table:
```
  k |      s
----+--------------
  0 | hello world
  1 | foo
  2 | bar
```

Would have the following statistics due to the encoding scheme (some
rows/columns omitted for brevity):
```
  statistics_name | column_names | row_count | distinct_count | null_count | average_row_size
------------------+--------------+-----------+----------------+------------+------------------
  __auto__        | {k}          |         0 |              0 |          0 |                0
  __auto__        | {s}          |         0 |              0 |          0 |                0
  NULL            | {k}          |         3 |              3 |          0 |                1
  NULL            | {s}          |         3 |              3 |          0 |                7
```

As part of this change, we also refactor some tests in `sampler_test.go`
and `sample_aggregator_test.go` to allow testing on a variable size type
(string) and on encoded data (bytes).

Fixes #55697

Release note (sql change): `system.table_statistics` has an additional
field, `avgSize`, that is the average size in bytes of the column(s)
with `columnIDs`. The new field is visible with the command
`SHOW STATISTICS FOR TABLE` and can be modified with the command
`INJECT STATISTICS`, as with other table statistics

issue_context.title: opt: table statistics should include information about the size of rows
issue_context.body:
Currently, the optimizer's statistics collector tracks the number of rows in a table, and histograms about the table's data distribution, but does not include information about the size of rows in a table.

This is troublesome for both costing and execution, because a row count estimate as exported by the optimizer is insufficient to make guesses about the amount of memory that a query might use, since rows are variably sized. The optimizer should collect, at minimum, an average data size per column as well, so that the coster and execution engine can make a guess at the amount of disk bytes that will be read by a query, and at the amount of memory that might need to be allocated for different parts of the query's execution.

There's a separate issue tracking optimizer changes: #72332

Epic: CRDB-10034



Jira issue: CRDB-13900
comments: #46560 is one example where this would be very useful.
I think the issue tracks also using these values in the optimizer (if not, we should open an issue for that).
There's a separate issue tracking optimizer changes: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/72332

review_comments: Thanks for adding this comment! Internal versions are independent from minor releases, a.k.a. patch releases, so this might be a bit misleading. We don't add internal versions in minor releases; internal releases should be thought of as the upgrade steps from one major release to another. If you find this confusing, you're not alone.

This change needs to be accompanied by a tenant migration, otherwise existing clusters, which already have a `table_statistics` table created before this change, will run into trouble when they're upgraded to a version which does include this change. I suspect that several CI failures are being caused by this missing migration.

Doing so involves adding a new internal version and key to `cockroach_versions.go` and binding a migration to it via a call to `migration.NewTenantMigration`. A good source of inspiration for how to do this and test it is `alter_web_sessions_create_indexes.go` which implements a similar migration.
